headline.title: A cyberattack forces New Mexico’s only Level-1 trauma center to divert ambulances
headline.quip: A whole state’s top trauma care ran through one hospital, and the hospital ran through one network. Single points of failure, nested.
headline.summary: A cyberattack on University of New Mexico Health led UNM Hospital, which runs the state’s only Level-1 trauma center, to divert all ambulances, restrict admissions and cancel clinic appointments and outpatient surgeries. Classes at four health-sciences colleges were cancelled. A group calling itself Byod claimed to have stolen data; UNM hasn’t confirmed this.

also.title: The Federal Election Commission’s e-filing goes dark
also.summary: E-filing at the US Federal Election Commission went down at about 10 p.m. ET after an email said a hacker was trying to breach its systems, and campaign spending reports couldn’t be filed. Reports put the outage at about 41 hours.
